name: Plate Table
subtitle: Parametric 1:10 construction mock
description: A dimension-driven apronless oak table with rounded tabletop and posts, four independently adjustable leveling feet, an optional rounded post-top groove, flush inset 6-inch corner plates, three recessed C-channels, and transparent geometry-only structural screening.

dimensionTargets: The full-size tabletop is 76 in long by 38 in wide by 1 1/2 in thick, and the finished table is 30 in high.

Four 4 in square posts use a separately adjustable outside corner radius and one shared radius for the other three vertical corners; both default to 1 in and meet a tabletop with 1 in plan-view corner radii.
The tabletop has 1/2 in top and bottom roundovers, leaving a 1/2 in flat vertical edge band.
Each post has an optional 1/4 in high by 1/8 in deep groove immediately below the tabletop; when enabled, the 1/4 in top roundover forms the lower shoulder of that groove.
Each post has a 1/4 in bottom roundover; disabling the groove restores the 1/4 in roundover to the post's top edge.
Four independently adjustable steel leveling feet default to 3/4 in installed extension, with one separately editable extension beneath each post.
Four 6 in square by 1/4 in steel plates are set 1/2 in back from both tabletop edges, and exactly three widthwise C-channels are flush with the tabletop underside.
The default 1:10 mock fits inside a 256 mm square printer bed footprint.
invariants: Keep the real furniture dimensions independent from the mock scale denominator.
Keep the tabletop and all four leg solids closed and printable.
Keep each post continuous; when the post-top groove is enabled, place the rounded shoulder below the recessed band rather than at the tabletop contact edge.
Keep the groove shallow enough to preserve a substantial post-to-tabletop bearing face.
Keep all four steel plate faces and three C-channel faces coplanar with the tabletop underside.
Keep every plate edge set back from the tabletop side and end so no steel is visible in a normal side elevation.
Keep the leg outer faces aligned to the tabletop edges when leg edge inset is zero.
Mirror the independently adjustable outside post corner to the matching outside corner at each of the four table positions.
Keep the three C-channel positions ordered from the first end of the table.
Keep top and bottom roundover radii within half the tabletop thickness.

When leveling feet are enabled, keep all four pads on the floor reference, preserve the tabletop height, shorten each wood post by its own installed extension, and retain positive threaded-rod embedment inside every post.

Expose a geometry-only structural screen for apronless post racking, plate-joint leverage, tabletop torsion, tipping, floor rocking, and member stiffness; never present it as load or joint certification.

Keep structural sensitivity monotonic: increasing overall height cannot improve the overall score, while increasing post size, plate size, or plate thickness cannot reduce their corresponding racking or joint score.

Export the wood and registered plate/C-channel/leveling-foot hardware as separate same-origin STL bodies, flipped with the tabletop top face on the build plate so the legs print upward without supports.
Treat oak grain and steel finish as render materials; dimensions come only from procedural geometry.
